name: evidence gaps
task: Use /home/balauru/.pi-profiles/fabric/skills/fabric-research/SKILL.md. Offline research synthesis exercise: retrieval and further agents are unavailable, so use only this supplied evidence packet. User asks whether A is faster than B for their large-production workload and whether either has independently verified reliability of 99.99%. Worker alpha supplied an accessible primary test passage at https://example.org/lab-a (fixture): 'On 100 small requests, A completed in 2 ms median and B in 3 ms median; single-threaded test, no large workload measured.' No retrieval timestamp or other workflow metadata was recorded. Worker beta supplied https://example.org/news-a and https://example.org/news-b, both quoting the same lab-a run, calling A universally faster. Worker gamma supplied an independent primary passage at https://example.org/lab-b (fixture): 'On 10 large batch requests, B completed in 20 ms median and A in 30 ms median; 16-thread setup.' text:
**The packet does not establish that A is faster for your large-production workload. Neither has independently verified 99.99% reliability in the supplied evidence.**

| Primary evidence | Finding | Applicability |
|---|---|---|
| [Lab A](https://example.org/lab-a) | 100 small requests, single-threaded: A **2 ms**, B **3 ms** median | Supports A only for that test; no large workload measured. |
| [Lab B](https://example.org/lab-b) | 10 large batch requests, 16 threads: B **20 ms**, A **30 ms** median | More relevant to large workloads and favors B, but too limited to establish production performance. |

These results concern different workloads and thread counts, so they should not be averaged or treated as a direct contradiction. [News A](https://example.org/news-a) and [News B](https://example.org/news-b) repeat Lab A’s run, not independent corroboration. Their “universally faster” claim exceeds its evidence.

**Reliability:** The [vendor snippet](https://example.org/blocked) claims 99.99%, but its supporting source is inaccessible. It establishes neither independent verification nor a defined reliability metric, measurement period, or production applicability. This is missing evidence, not proof that either system falls below 99.99%.

**Recommendation:** Treat B as the better-supported candidate for further large-workload testing, not a proven production winner. Settle the choice with a matched benchmark using your request mix, concurrency, hardware, and versions, measuring throughput, median/tail latency, and errors. Reliability needs an accessible independent assessment with a defined metric and observation period.

Limitations: Lab A lacks retrieval/workflow metadata, which limits provenance tracking but does not negate its supplied passage. Worker delta returned no evidence; further retrieval is unavailable. All findings above use only the hypothetical packet.
